<string name="ring_row_description">A glow around the camera hole while the screen is off</string>

<string name="ring_intro">When a notification arrives and the screen is off, a ring lights up around the camera hole in the app\'s colour, with the waiting apps below it. <string name="ring_enable_description">Only notifications you could dismiss; nothing for downloads, playback or apps running in the background.</string>
<string name="ring_access_missing">Not granted — the ring cannot see notifications</string>
<string name="ring_fullscreen_missing">Not allowed — the ring cannot turn the screen on</string>
<string name="ring_post_missing">Blocked — the ring is announced through a silent notification you never see</string>
<string name="ring_grant_pairing_hint">Pair wireless debugging once on the Keyboard backlight screen and every permission here is granted without a trip into system settings.</string>

<string name="ring_duration_description">After this the ring lets go and the phone\'s own timeout turns the screen off. Longer costs battery: the panel is on, even if almost all of it is black.</string>

<string name="density_stock">The density this screen shipped with</string>

<string name="bloat_row_description">Disable or uninstall the Unihertz apps Android won\'t let you remove</string>

<string name="bloat_intro">Unihertz ships apps that cannot be removed the normal way. PhysiBoard already has the wireless-debugging access it uses for the keyboard backlight, so it can disable or uninstall them for you — and put every one of them back.</string>
<string name="bloat_wrong_device">This list was written for the Titan 2 Elite and stays switched off on other phones, because it removes packages by name.</string>
<string name="bloat_not_paired">Needs the same wireless-debugging pairing as the keyboard backlight.</string>

<string name="bloat_preset_factory_description">Production-line tooling: burn-in and hardware tests, sensor calibration, an IMEI writer, a RAM tester, a GPS checker and a couple of packages that were never meant to ship. None of it has an icon, none of it does anything for a phone that has left the factory. The safest set here.</string>

<string name="bloat_preset_vendor_description">Unihertz\'s own convenience apps — a toolbox, game mode, bedtime, a pedometer, rotation control, a cycling speedometer, a call recorder and an NFC helper. These are real features, so this one is taste rather than safety. App Lock, Private Space and Student Mode are deliberately left out in case you rely on them, and the IR Remote is never touched because it drives the infrared blaster.</string>

<string name="bloat_preset_privacy_description">Packages that report or record: battery telemetry for the vendor, carrier APN details, a chipset logger that writes continuously, and automatic call recording. Some of these also appear in the sets above — a package can be factory tooling and a privacy question at the same time.</string>

<string name="bloat_preset_description">Unihertz ships several tools whose job is stopping background apps from running: a phone manager, an app freezer, a blocker, a junk cleaner and a chipset logger that writes constantly. Android Auto is a long-running session, which is exactly what those interrupt.\n\nWorth being straight with you: this is the most likely cause of Android Auto dropping, not a proven one. What is certain is what these apps do. Disabling is reversible, which is what makes it worth trying.</string>
<string name="bloat_unknown_title">%1$d vendor apps not in this list</string>

<string name="bloat_unknown_description">Every Titan 2 Elite ships identically, so these came from a firmware update after this list was written — or this is not a Titan 2 Elite. Shown, not touched: an app nobody has checked is not one to remove.</string>
<string name="bloat_tier_safe_blurb">Test and calibration apps left over from the production line. Nothing uses them.</string>
<string name="bloat_tier_optional_blurb">Real features that duplicate something Android already does, or that you may simply not want.</string>
<string name="bloat_tier_useful_blurb">Listed so you can see them, but removing these makes real hardware stop working.</string>

<string name="bloat_uninstall_confirm_message">Disabling is usually enough: it hides the app and stops it running, and is instantly reversible.
